Hand-authored to mirror docs/web/ASSET-SPECS.md. Deliberately NOT generated
from the build scripts: a checker derived from the builder only ever proves
the builder agrees with itself.
dims_xyz_m are in THREE.JS axes (X right, Y up, Z forward) after the
Blender +Z-up -> glTF +Y-up conversion, so a Blender footprint of
(X=1.0, Y=1.0 flow, Z=0.30 tall) is written here as [1.0, 0.30, 1.0].
Checking it in three.js axes is what proves export_yup actually fired.
Run: python tools/blender/validate_glb.py --all
RN-1620: THE `max_px` CEILING ON THE TWO CARD FAMILIES, 256 -> 1024, AND
WHY THE BUDGET ROW IS THE FIX RATHER THAN THE MESH. Ten assets failed
validate_glb (bush_scrub, detail_cards, props_beach/canopy/forest/hills/
ocean/plains, tree_broadleaf, tree_conifer) on 28 identical rows, and the
message was the same one every time: `family 'leaf' size_px 1024 > max_px
256`. Not ten defects. ONE, with ten symptoms, and it is in this file.
RN-1500 (commit b8d3a2f, 2026-08-13) raised `leaf` and `grass` from 256 px
to 1024 px under D-020 decision 4's general raise, edited texgen.py's
ALBEDO_FAMILIES, RE-MEASURED both coverage bands against the new output
rather than carrying the 256 px numbers over, and regenerated
surfaces.json. It did not revisit these declarations, which were written
by RN-179/RN-180 (commit 1122f47) back when 256 was the truth. So this
file has been asserting a ceiling that a decided, argued, shipped raise
deliberately exceeded, and it went red the moment that raise landed.
THE DIRECTION OF THE FIX IS THE WHOLE QUESTION and it has one answer.
Lowering the families back to 256 would revert a logged decision on the
strength of a stale number, and it would revert it BADLY: the RN-1500
shape edits (grass's narrowed blades, leaf's root flare) were authored
and their alpha-coverage re-bracketed against 1024 px output, so the old
256 px bands no longer describe the cards that exist. The families are
right and the ceiling is old, so the ceiling moves.
WHAT IT COSTS, STATED. Two cards, 1024^2 RGBA, ~5.3 MiB each with mips,
~10.7 MiB for the pair, against 0.4 MiB at 256. That is the price D-020
decision 4 already accepted; this row is not re-deciding it, it is
stopping the gate from disagreeing with it. The ladder these ceilings now
describe is texgen's own: 384/512 for the tiling families, 1024 for the
two alpha cards, and 2048 reserved for `panel` alone.
NOT A BLANKET RAISE. Every `max_px` in this file is a leaf or grass row;
no tiling family's ceiling moved, and a future 2048 card would fail here
again, which is the ratchet doing its job.
RN-1624. WHAT IS LEFT WHERE A BUILDING USED TO STAND, and it pays a
debt that was booked with its own placeholder flag. D1 shipped
destruction with `assets/nodes/boulder_stone.glb` squashed to 0.45 and
scaled to whatever fell, and `Wreckage.report()` published
`meshIsPlaceholder: true` so nobody had to guess. That flag is now
false and this is why.
THREE AUTHORED SIZES, NOT ONE MESH SCALED. Wreckage.SPAN_M runs 0.70 m
(power pole) to 8.00 m (launch pad); one asset across that is stretched
by ELEVEN, which destroys every authored proportion in it - plate gauge,
shard size, how far a beam protrudes. Small 0.90 / Med 2.20 / Large 3.40
bracket the table so every kind but the launch pad lands inside 1.45x of
an authored size, and the client picks the nearest rather than either
side re-deriving the other's numbers.
THE THREE ARE DIFFERENT WRECKS, not one arrangement at three scales:
a bent deck and frame (belt), plate and studs (wall), broken slab with
reinforcement standing out of it (foundation). A player who has
demolished twenty things must not be able to see they were one model.
NO `collision` KEY, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Wreckage.ts gives the
reason: 'the part is gone' is only a real claim if the walker can now
cross where it stood, and a rubble collider would make that claim
untestable and the feature indistinguishable from the bug.
probes/destruction.js inverts the CE-50 occupancy technique on exactly
this. So the asset ships NO col_ node - the same shape detail_cards,
vfx_engine_plume and body_sphere_lod already have - and a proxy added
here would break a shipped probe's assertion rather than add weight.
THE DECLARED BOX IS OWNED BY NAMED PARTS, the discipline the miner's
foot pads and the belt's rail ends already follow: two unyawed mounds
own X and Y exactly and the CREST plate owns the height, so the pivot
is centred by construction rather than by subtracting a measured
offset back out. mf.assert_inside refuses the build if anything else
reaches the box, so a failure is caught where it is caused.
max_materials 5: SteelDark intact plate, Steel members, SteelRust the
TORN faces and cut ends (texgen's `rust` is steel that has GONE, and
wreckage is the one place in this game where that is literal), Rock

the cheapest part of the asset and the loudest, because paint is
manufactured and nothing in nature is that colour.
THE SHADOW LADDER EARNS ALMOST NOTHING AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER
THAN QUIETLY LEFT. check_shadow_lod: Small LOD1 109.62 mm (c2, 3.0x),
Med 317.59 and Large 514.43 (no cascade, 4.0x). The cause was measured,
not guessed: LOD1 drops the debris field, and the shards scatter into
the footprint DIAGONALS where the four axis-aligned apron sheets have
nothing. Deepening the sheets was tried and moved Med 317.59 -> 216.55
and Large not at all, so it was reverted.
IT IS RN-1599's POWER-POLE LESSON IN PROP FORM, and that is why no
further iteration was spent: a machine's detail is CONCENTRATED, so one
stand-in box catches it (the miner's guard cage, RN-1623); a pile of
twenty-five scattered small solids has no large-scale mass to
approximate at all - it IS its details - so a proxy that earns a
cascade would have to reproduce the debris field, which is LOD0 again.
The bill is 4 x 372 = 1,488 triangles for the worst pile, and piles
exist only where a building was destroyed, which is a handful and not
the fifty-seven belts a raise on the belt tile is priced against.
LOD1 is still worth shipping on SCREEN distance alone: it is 32 per
cent cheaper than LOD0 and it is what a pile looks like at range.
RN-1563 to RN-1565, THE SE FORM PASS, and this is the raise in this wave
that needs the most argument, because a belt is the most numerous object
in a factory: portcost's reference base carries 57 of them against 22
smelters and no assembler at all. lod0 200 to 360 (actual 340), total 420
to 610 (actual 568), max_materials 4 to 5.
WHAT THE TRIANGLES BOUGHT, and they all went to one place. The only part
of a belt tile a player can ever see is the two 1.00 x 0.30 rail faces on
the cell edge, the deck from above, and the 0.10 m gap between one
under-frame and the next. Each rail was ONE extruded box. It is now a
fabricated section: flanges on the edge, a 15 mm lightening pocket
between them, a mid-span stiffener and solid full-section end blocks,
plus the splice plate and bolts a modular tile joins its neighbour with.
+192 tris x 57 belts is +10,944 against the reference base's 660,385,
i.e. +1.66 per cent of the whole scene, spent on the object the player
watches cargo ride along all game.
THE POCKET IS 15 mm BECAUSE CASCADE 0 IS 15.47 mm PER TEXEL. LOD1 is
still one solid box per rail, every new LOD0 vertex is within one shadow
texel of it, and all three cascades keep drawing the 108-triangle proxy
instead of promoting the 340-triangle mesh. A deeper pocket would have
looked no different and cost cascade 0 the whole LOD0 on every belt.
THE TILE ENDS STAY SOLID FULL-SECTION so a straight tile butted against a
curve has the same seam it always had: belt_curve_common.py shares this
file's rail width and deck height precisely so that junction is
invisible, and its rail is still one solid arc band.

THE METHOD, because it is reusable and the smelter is still owed it.
Every LOD0 feature standing over one shadow texel from the tier is
blocked in at its ENVELOPE, one box per feature, and the envelopes are
MEASURED - traced out of of_lib.MeshBuilder._add over this file's own
LOD0 build - rather than eyeballed. The metric is distance to the
NEAREST surface point, so a part only needs one coordinate on a face
of the box containing it, which is why a flat ring like the drill
collar is answered honestly by a slab of its own thickness. The one
case that breaks is a part interior in all three axes: the junction
box's four lid bolts, which needed a second thin plate at their own
layer and were the last 63.20 mm in the way.
THE GUARD CAGE WAS THE HEADLINE AT 622 mm AND ITS RING IS 8-SEGMENT
ON PURPOSE. `guard_cage` lays bars with ring_boxes at 2*pi*i/8 and
rolls hoops from arc_ring at segs=8, so both sit on an 8-fold lattice;
a proxy ring on that same lattice puts every bar and hoop vertex on a
facet CORNER at full radius instead of at a midpoint where a coarse
ring sags away. 72 triangles where an unaligned ring needed 136.

method: block in every LOD0 feature standing over one shadow texel

and exact vertex bounds of every LOD0 primitive, each group was
checked against LOD1's own surface with check_shadow_lod's own
nearest-surface metric, and every box added is that measured bound,
not an eyeballed one. 27 features were still proud past 56.25 mm:
the stack's flared foot and cleanout (this tier had neither), the
roof junction box, the hood's mounting brackets, the firebox
coaming/hinges/latch/peep, both port throat plates, the louvre, the
step tread, the ladder's own rungs (the block already here only
carried the stringers and landing), the service duct, the gauge
cluster and hatch, the status bezel, four cable trays, the anchor
pads and the body ribs (this tier's shell has none).

the junction box's own four lid bolts sit deep inside the combined
housing+plate+bolt envelope in every axis - RN-1623's junction box
lid bolts again - and needed a SECOND thin plate at the bolts' own

THE VESSEL PART CATALOGUE (DW-29), and the TWO-CLASS STACK CONTRACT.
Twenty-three parts in one file, one group node each, so a renderer
clones the PART and gets its meshes, its sockets and its proxy
together.
TWO DIAMETER CLASSES AND NO MORE. Class S is 1.25 m (R 0.625, 16
segments) and class L is 2.50 m (R 1.250, 24 segments), exactly 2x.
A segment count divisible by 4 puts vertices on +-X and +-Y, so the
exported AABB is exactly the class diameter; a 14-gon at R 0.625
measures 1.250 x 1.244 and misses by 6 mm.
Seventeen stack parts are ground-pivoted on their bottom mating
plane, so socket_stack_bottom is always the origin and stacking is
one addition per part, with no per-part offset table anywhere.
StackAdapter is the ONE part whose two ends differ in class: bottom
L, top S. Without it two classes would be two disjoint catalogues.
Six radial parts (radial decoupler, vernier, fin, RCS, leg, solar
panel) have their origin on their MOUNT PLANE with the body
extending +X, which is neither 'ground' nor 'centre': pivot 'none'
and the dimensions are the check.
SolidBooster is carried radially but is NOT a radial part: it is a
stack part with a socket_radial_attach on its own hull, which mates
with RadialDecoupler's socket_radial_out. Same anti-parallel dot
product as a stack mate, so one rule covers both.
The landing leg and the solar panel are authored STOWED, because the
exported static pose is frame 1 of the deploy clip and a vessel
flies stowed. Each splits into a fixed mesh and an animated one,
because one Blender Action drives one object.
part_sockets is the real gate here: twenty parts carry a
socket_stack_top between them, so a flat presence check proves
nothing. It asserts each socket is under ITS part and lands on the
declared point in three.js axes.
LOD0 only, deliberately: a vessel is either near you or it is a
scaled-scene impostor, and there is no middle band for a part.

relationship written in prose is a number nobody is checking, and the
socket_frames block below is the check.

THE BUDGETS, ARGUED FROM MULTIPLICITY AND FROM THE FRAME. LOD0 measures
15,920 and is capped at 16,200; the three tiers total 25,848 against
27,000. The two anchors in this file are the space station (17,600 LOD0,
72,000 total, multiplicity 1, and drawn in an ORBITAL frame with no
terrain LOD0 ring, no detail cards and no factory) and the wall (240 /
340, multiplicity in the thousands). The ruin sits between them and is
priced from where: poi.h places ONE today (forgeSpecs count 1, variants
1) and Reid's ruling is more scattered later, so about ten eventually,
but they are scattered over a planet at a 700 to 1400 m band from an
anchor and stream in on approach, so the SIMULTANEOUS count in a frame is
one, rarely two. Against RN-71's measured 555k to 1.0 M triangle surface
frame, and at the MEASURED 2.0x marginal multiplier, one ruin costs
LOD0 plus two cascades of LOD1 = 28,320 triangles, or 2.8 to 5.1 per
cent of a frame it DOES share with terrain, flora and machines; LOD0
alone is 1.6 to 2.9 per cent. Had the ladder shipped at the 4.0x it
first measured, the same asset would have cost 63,680, which is where
a budget argument becomes a shadow-LOD argument. ART-DIRECTION.md makes
raising a budget a normal arguable act and this is the argument: 9,720
of LOD0's triangles are greebles at or under `hinge` that LOD1 drops
entirely, i.e. they are close-range surface detail on the one asset in
the game a player is asked to walk inside and stand still in, which is
exactly what 'something to look at up close' costs.
COLLISION IS THE FEATURE, BECAUSE ENTERABLE IS THE BRIEF. 41 proxies out
of one collision_boxes() function: floors, walls and ceilings separately,
because one enclosing box cannot describe an interior and would make the
ruin a solid lump. R48 governs the overhead set - there is no ceiling
authority in the walker, only free() with three point samples 0.75 m
apart, so a horizontal proxy thinner than 0.75 m fits between two samples
and the player walks through it - and every overhead proxy here is
0.80 m. The cella's ceiling is three boxes WITH THE HOLE IN IT rather
than one that plasters over it, because the hole is where the light and
the rain come in and a proxy set that disagreed with the picture is the
state in which nobody notices anything else. The round deck is the union
of seven axis-aligned rectangles with their corners on the circle, spaced
by build_space_station.hall_steps's closed form (GP-400), which stops the
player 1.1057 m short of the visible edge: the SAME stand-off the station
shipped, at twice the radius, for four more boxes.
THERE IS NO STAIR AND THAT IS A REFUSAL WITH A CAUSE. Three treads at a
walkable 0.48 m going project 1.44 m out from the stylobate face, putting
stone at radius 18.56 m: outside the 18.0 m footprintM that admit()
measured the ground flatness over, so the stair would stand on terrain
nothing ever checked. Recessing it is not available because nothing in
this project cuts geometry. So the stair is robbed out - the two cheek
blocks survive with the tread sockets of a flight that is gone - and the
player climbs the 1.00 m stylobate directly on CAPSULE.stepUpM 1.10.
The consequence for the placement lane: on a steeply admitted site the
downhill rim stands up to 3.26 m proud, so the ruin is enterable from its
uphill side and not from every side, by construction.
EIGHT MATERIALS, AND EACH NAMES A STATE RATHER THAN A COLOUR: Rock is
weathered ashlar, RockDark is sheltered stone and water staining, Sand is
FRESHLY BROKEN stone (a chip exposes pale unweathered interior, so
authoring spall in the wall's own role would make it invisible), Soil is
silt banked against the stone, LeafDeep is cushion moss in full shade
and LeafDry is crustose lichen in the half-shaded band (an olive-tan;
`Grass` shipped here first and was pulled after the renders, because a
saturated mid-green authored for ground cover at range reads as a
painted panel at 0.3 m on grey stone, which is exactly the saturated
primary ART-DIRECTION.md names as a failure), Copper is the builders'
bronze cramps and the stele's inlay,
and Coal is stone blackened where the fire was hottest. Every role is
already in of_lib.PALETTE, so this build opened no shared file: not
of_lib.py, not texgen.py, not surfaces.json. OF_LeafDeep and OF_LeafDry
are in of_lib.DOUBLE_SIDED and are declared below.
EVERY WEAR MARK IS TWO OVERLAPPING BOXES AND NOT ONE RECTANGLE, which
is a correction taken off the first renders rather than off a gate.
Every mark passed validate_glb.py and check_shadow_lod.py and looked
like a POSTER: one axis-aligned box 19 to 31 mm proud of a flat face,
hard rectangular outline, flat contrasting colour, reading as signage
stuck to the stone rather than as damage in it. `clean is now a defect`
cuts both ways - a crisp rectangle of dirt is as clean as no dirt. A
second smaller box on the layer BELOW, offset about a third of the main
one, breaks the outline and doubles the edges that catch a grazing
light, at 24 triangles a mark instead of 12; the counts feeding it were
roughly halved, so the same triangles buy half as many marks each of
which is worth looking at. The satellite is always on a SHALLOWER layer
than its parent, so the shadow ladder is untouched and LOD1 still
measures 50.76 mm after the change.
EVERY WEAR MARK HAS A CAUSE AND THE CAUSES ARE FIELDS, NOT DECALS.
damage(x, y) is one falloff from a point off the +X / -Y quarter and it
decides pier state, blackening, rubble placement and spall depth, so the
+X / -Y corner is flattened, the -X / +Y side stands, and the surviving
colonnade is contiguous (which is what lets an entablature exist at all:
9 full piers, 3 snapped, 5 stumps, 7 surviving spans). Rubble sits under
the spans that are GONE. A drip stain is emitted below a surviving
cornice and nowhere else, so where the cornice is broken the stain stops
dead. shade() is a dot product against one authored sun bearing, and
inside the cella the only growth is the one patch under the hole in the
roof, because that is the only place light and water both arrive.
sag_beam bows the architrave's own soffit over its span rather than
rotating a straight block, which is the difference between a beam that
has crept and one that has not.
THE RESEARCH STATION: the field bench D-019 minted a TypeId for on
2026-08-11 and gave no mesh, so ResearchStations.ts drew
machines/assembler.glb until this landed. Built by
tools/blender/build_research_station.py on station_form.Panel and
machine_form's greeble vocabulary.
EVERY DIMENSION IS DERIVED FROM THE CLIENT AND NOT FROM THE ASSET IT
REPLACED. The assembler is 8.00 m square; the class that borrowed it
snaps to MachinePlacement.MACHINE_TILE_M = 1.00 m, places 2.20 m
ahead of the eye and picks with a 1.40 m sphere sitting 0.70 m up,
i.e. it describes something a person stands at. The footprint is
2.00 x 2.00 (two tiles, so two benches on adjacent cells abut
exactly) and the height 2.44 m is SOLVED from the pick: the mast
stands 0.721 m out in plan, so ResearchStations.pick's own
STATION_RADIUS_M + 0.5 = 1.90 m sphere allows it
sqrt(1.90^2 - 0.721^2) = 1.757 m above the sphere centre, i.e.
z <= 2.4578. MEASURED: the worst LOD0 vertex is 1.8894 m from that
centre, so EVERY PART OF THIS ASSET IS SELECTABLE, which is a
property contracts.json cannot express (it measures a box and this is
a sphere) and which build_research_station._assert_envelope therefore
checks off the accumulated vertices and refuses the build over.
THE DECK PLATE OWNS THE BOUNDING BOX, build_ruin.py's resolution of
the same fight between the `ground` pivot's centred-AABB demand and
ART-DIRECTION.md's asymmetry. The 2.00 x 2.00 x 0.06 skid deck is
exactly centred and is the only element allowed to reach 1.00 m;
everything else is asserted inside KEEP = 0.94, so the cabinet can
sit in the +Y half, the bench and console in the -Y half and the mast
in the +X quarter with nothing mirrored anywhere. The rule is stated
as a BAND IN Z rather than as `the skid`, so a runner, a foot pad or a
rubbing strip that crept outward is caught: the first build put the
levelling pads at HALF - 0.14 and their 0.11 m rims reached 0.97.
+Y IS THE BACK AND -Y IS WHERE THE PLAYER STANDS. ResearchStations.
faceToward yaws the group until three.js local +Z points at the eye,
and of_lib exports Blender (x, y, z) as glTF (x, z, -y), so glTF +Z
is Blender -Y. Screen, gauges, control shelf, bench, drawer and kick
plate are all on -Y; hatch, junction box, cable tray and earth spike
are all on +Y.
THE LADDER IS MEASURED. Every optional detail is a station_form.Panel
part taking its proud height from machine_form.LAYER, so a tier's
worst deviation is decided by which layers it drops rather than
discovered afterwards. LOD1 takes min_layer `clip` 0.061 and drops
every greeble at or under `hinge` 0.052; LOD2 takes `bracket` 0.232
and additionally omits the services stage, so it is a SCREEN-DISTANCE
tier and is stated as one. check_shadow_lod.py measures LOD1 at
50.76 mm and LOD2 at 232.00 mm: LOD1 earns cascades 1 and 2, the
three cascades draw tiers 0, 1, 1, and the marginal multiplier is
2.0x. Nothing here reaches cascade 0's 15.47 mm, so there was never a
third rung to compete for.
TWO LAYER CHOICES ARE CORRECTIONS TAKEN OFF THE FIRST BUILD AND NOT
OFF A GATE. The screen backlight was on `scribe` (6 mm) and the pane
on `plate` (24 mm), both under LOD1's threshold, so the one feature
the whole asset exists for switched off at the first LOD band - and
of_lib.report's own role list showed it, because LOD1 shipped without
OF_EmissiveState at all. They are now `tray` (74 mm) and `grille`
(98 mm), the shallowest layers above the threshold that still leave
the coaming (108 mm) proud of the glass, and the status lamp moved
with them. THE LIT PLATE ITSELF is then emitted at every tier as plain
structure, at exactly the coordinates `tray` gives it so LOD0 and LOD1
are unchanged to the vertex: LOD2's `bracket` threshold would otherwise
switch the screen OFF at the range at which a lit panel is most of what
the asset says. An emissive is not a greeble. The hazard mark on the loader corner had the same problem
and the opposite fix: a painted stripe honestly belongs on `plate`,
so the striping is backed by a BOLTED STEEL ANGLE emitted at every
tier, which is a real part rather than a layer exception.
THE BUDGET, ARGUED FROM MULTIPLICITY. LOD0 measures 2,860 against a
3,200 cap and the three tiers total 5,748 against 6,400. The anchors
are the assembler (3,050 LOD0 over 8 x 8 m, and many of them in a
factory) and the ruin (15,920 over 35 m, one on the planet). GP-615
gates the research SCREEN on a built station, so a player needs
exactly ONE and has no reason to build a second: the simultaneous
count in a frame is one. Against RN-71's measured 555k to 1.0 M
triangle surface frame, one station at the measured 2.0x marginal
multiplier costs 2,860 + 2 x 1,852 = 6,564 triangles, which is 0.7 to
1.2 per cent of a frame. A bench the player walks up to and reads a
screen on is the definition of ART-DIRECTION.md's `something to look
at up close`, and 1,008 of LOD0's triangles are greebles at or under
`hinge` that LOD1 drops entirely.
COLLISION IS FOUR BOXES AND THE BENCH IS SOLID TO THE GROUND. The
walker is a LINE with three samples at 0.15 / 0.90 / 1.65 m and no
radius (R48), so a 0.09 m bench slab at 0.92 m is sampled by exactly
one of them and missed by a player standing 60 mm higher up a slope.
The skid proxy is 0.24 m and is deliberately steppable against
CAPSULE.stepUpM 1.10: a pallet is a thing you step onto.
EIGHT ROLES, EVERY ONE ALREADY IN of_lib.PALETTE AND ALREADY IN ALL
THREE TABLES check-roles.mjs COMPARES, so this build opened no shared
file: not of_lib.py, not texgen.py, not surfaces.json, not
Surfaces.ts. Steel is the coated sheet, SteelDark the skid and every
structural member, SteelLight the machined and bright fittings,
Accent the instrument fascia and rating plates, Hazard the corner
angle, Rubber the conduit and the cable hank, Glass the screen pane
and the sky dome, EmissiveState the backlight behind that pane and
the status lamp. OF_Glass is in of_lib.DOUBLE_SIDED and is declared
below. The screen is Glass at alpha 0.35 OVER an emissive plate
rather than one emissive rectangle, because a lit plate read through
glass with the bezel on top is what a display looks like and one
emissive rectangle is a lamp.
THE SCANNING ANTENNA: GP-533's seventh survival::StructureKind, which
shipped on 2026-08-13 with a price, a tech, a save path, a 2,500 m
POI reveal and machines/power_pole.glb for a mesh. Built by
tools/blender/build_scanning_antenna.py.
WHAT IT HAS TO SAY FROM A HUNDRED METRES is `this is the machine that
looked around`, and the two shapes that say it without a caption are
a DISH and a GUYED MAST. Both are authored: a 2.10 m panelled
paraboloid on an elevation trunnion with a feed horn on a quadripod
at the focus and four ribs behind it, on a four-chord lattice tower
with N-braced diagonals, on a plinth, held by four guys to four
ground anchors. A LATTICE IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR READING AGAINST
THE SKY: a tube is a silhouette and a lattice is a silhouette with
sky through it, and the diagonals change with bearing as the player
walks round it.
station_form.antenna EXISTS AND WAS REFUSED, which is worth recording
because reuse is the default rule. It is a mast box plus a fan of
eight ONE-SIDED triangles round a cone, correct for a 400 km hull
silhouette the player flies past. It has no thickness, no rim, no
ribs, no feed and no mount, and because OF_SteelLight is backface
culled it renders as a hole in the world when seen from behind - which
is roughly half the time a player walks round a thing standing on the
ground. The reflector here is a CLOSED solid (front skin, back skin,
outer rim, inner rim) wound by mf.oriented off the signed volume.
THE FOUR ANCHORS OWN THE BOUNDING BOX AND THAT IS WHY THERE ARE FOUR.
The `ground` pivot wants a centred AABB and ART-DIRECTION.md wants
asymmetry; the ruin gives the box to its buried course and the
research station to its skid deck. Four identical anchor blocks at
four corners is not a compromise with the validator, it is what a
guyed mast IS, and it buys everything else the freedom to be
lopsided: the equipment cabinet is on one side only, the feeder
climbs one chord only, the rungs are on one face only, and the dish
hangs entirely into the -Y half. The blocks are 0.44 square at
(+-1.28, +-1.28) so their outer faces land on +-1.50 exactly, and
everything else is asserted inside KEEP = 1.42. THE YELLOW IS
STRUCTURE, a capping course rather than paint: the first build used
`scribe` stripes on the outboard faces, which stood 6 mm proud (AABB
3.006) and, being below LOD1's threshold, would have given the three
tiers DIFFERENT bounding boxes. The anchor bolts moved from 0.15 to
0.11 off centre for the same reason.
HEIGHT IS SOLVED BACKWARDS. The topmost point of the asset is the
reflector rim at the top of the bowl, (DISH_R + DEPTH) * sin(45) above
the vertex, so TRUNNION_Z = 6.00 - that, = 5.0255. Both LOD sector
counts (16 and 8) put a vertex at exactly theta = 90 degrees, which is
what lets all three tiers share one dims_xyz_m. The dish is f/D 0.40
(focal 0.840 m, depth 0.3281 m) and is aimed at -Y, i.e. AT the player
who placed it and over their head, because ResearchStations.faceToward
turns glTF +Z (Blender -Y) toward the eye and a dish facing away would
show its back for ever.
THE PICK SPHERE DOES NOT REACH THE HEAD, MEASURED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.
Antennas.pick is ResearchStations.pick verbatim - a 1.40 m sphere
0.70 m up, plus 0.50 m of slack - so it refuses any ray whose
perpendicular distance from (0, 0, 0.70) exceeds 1.90 m. On the 2.44 m
bench that is satisfiable and the build asserts it vertex by vertex;
on a 6 m mast it is not, and satisfying it would mean building a
2.6 m antenna. MEASURED: 57.0 per cent of LOD0 vertices lie inside
the sphere and on the mast axis selection stops at z = 2.555. What
this means in play is that a LEVEL crosshair at eye height 1.60 m
scores |1.60 - 0.70| = 0.90 m against the 1.90 m limit at any range,
so aiming at the tower works and aiming at the dish does not. The
borrowed power_pole.glb had the identical property at 4.0 m and
nobody had measured it. Widening ANTENNA_RADIUS_M is a gameplay
change and is left to that lane rather than taken by an art lane.
THE LADDER. LOD1 takes min_layer `clip` 0.061, dropping every greeble
at or under `hinge` 0.052, and keeps the dish at 16 sectors:
check_shadow_lod.py measures 50.76 mm, so it earns cascades 1 and 2
and the marginal multiplier is 2.0x. LOD2 takes `bracket` 0.232 AND
three structural savings the layer ladder would refuse - the dish
drops to 8 sectors, half the tower diagonals go, the guy turnbuckles
go and the quadripod loses two legs. An 8-gon reflector sits
r(1 - cos(180/8)) = 80 mm inside a 16-gon one, so this tier CANNOT be
shadow-safe: it MEASURES 209.98 mm, which happens to fall just inside
cascade 2's 210.94 mm texel, and that is a coincidence rather than a
design and is not relied on anywhere. It is a screen-distance tier,
stated in advance rather than discovered afterwards, which is
build_ruin.py's own correction to build_space_station.py.
THE BUDGET. LOD0 measures 2,848 against a 3,200 cap and the three
tiers total 6,688 against 7,400. GP-536 makes the reveal idempotent
(of_poi_mark_known returning false), so a second antenna EXTENDS
coverage rather than double-counting and a player has a real reason
to build two or three across a base's spread - the simultaneous count
is one or two, not one. At the measured 2.0x marginal multiplier two
antennas cost 2 x (2,848 + 2 x 2,272) = 14,784 triangles against
RN-71's 555k to 1.0 M surface frame, 1.5 to 2.7 per cent. The lattice
is where the triangles went: 900 of LOD0's are the tower's chords,
ties and diagonals, and they are what stops it reading as a pole.
COLLISION IS SEVEN BOXES. Plinth, mast and cabinet plus one per
anchor: the anchors are 0.26 m and steppable against CAPSULE.stepUpM
1.10, but they are solid, because a guy anchor a player walks
through is the state in which nobody trusts any collider on the
asset. Naming is col_Anchor1..4 rather than col_Anchor_1..4 on
purpose: check-proxies.mjs catalogues the three.js `Name_<digits>`
trap, where a proxy genuinely named col_Step_1 silently deletes
col_Step_2 and everything after it.
EIGHT ROLES, ALL ALREADY IN of_lib.PALETTE AND IN ALL THREE TABLES
check-roles.mjs COMPARES, so this build opened no shared file. Steel
is the cabinet sheet, SteelDark every structural member, SteelLight
the reflector skin and the bright fittings, Accent the fascia and
placards, Hazard the anchor capping course, Rubber the feeder and
conduit, EmissiveState the obstruction light and the cabinet lamp,
and Copper is the two places a real installation is not painted
steel: the waveguide and feed collar, and the earth bonding braid.
Nothing here is double sided.
NO CLIPS, AND THAT IS A REFUSAL. A slowly rotating dish is the
obvious animation and nothing in the client would play it: Antennas.ts
clones the template, calls selectLod and never touches
AnimationMixer, and a declared clip that nothing drives is dead bytes
plus a row in this file that reads like a feature. The elevation
screw jack under the dish's back rib is the static version of the
same statement - it says the thing points somewhere - and it costs
two boxes.
